title: MEPS 2023: people with a reported ICD-10 A69 (other spirochetal infections, which includes Lyme disease)
definition: People with at least one condition record whose 3-character ICD10CDX equals A69.
method: Sum of unique-person weights (PERWT23F) over the domain; standard error by Taylor linearisation over VARSTR/VARPSU. Person-level, one year only.
comparability: A69 is the broad category that contains Lyme (A69.2x); MEPS public files keep only the first 3 characters, so this is NOT a Lyme-specific count and must not be read as Lyme prevalence.
MEPS panels overlap across adjacent years: never add or pool these yearly totals.
Condition rows come from household reports coded by professional coders.
Not a zero: the code is withheld under MEPS confidentiality rules (N must be at least 30), so absence says nothing about whether cases existed.
summary: 2023: code A69 does not appear in the public file. AHRQ states that a 3-digit code is released only when at least 30 sampled persons carry it, so the true sample count is between 0 and 29; no estimate or standard error can be formed.
how_to_use: Context only: explains why this year has no Lyme-related (A69) figure.

provenance.collection_note: Respondent-reported conditions and hours, coded to ICD-10 by MEPS abstractors; not a clinical record.
provenance.computed_by: Computed in code from the federal file; no AI model
